answer: Require every agent to post a bond that can be slashed when its actions expose coordinated fraud—for example, when several newly funded accounts repeat the same rare transaction pattern and fail independent challenge tasks. A graph of trusted, costly interactions creates a ripple: one proven fake can taint its funder and bridge accounts, triggering review rather than automatic guilt. A sable-colored profile or fresh key earns no trust by itself. To scale a sybil, an attacker must lock up capital, build credible history, and risk losing bonds across linked identities.
